The '''Grizmallt nerf'''<ref name="DB">{{DB|creature|nerf|nerf}}</ref> was a rare [[Species/Legends|subspecies]] of [[Nerf/Legends|nerf]]&mdash;a [[Sentience/Legends|nonsentient]] species&mdash;that lived on<ref name="Alien" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]]. The subspecies featured a variety of differences to common [[Alderaanian/Legends|Alderaanian]] nerfs,<ref name="Alien" /> as they were significantly taller and slimmer,<ref name="DB" /> having more resemblance to [[Eopie/Legends|eopies]] with antlers. It was speculated in [[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species (book)|''The New Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], an [[Sentientologist|anthropological]] text compiled from the notes of [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]], that the nerfs on Grizmallt had evolved in body shape and neck length through thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of reaching up to [[Tree/Legends|trees]] to [[Diet/Legends|eat]] [[Berry/Legends|berries]] and leaves.<ref name="Alien" /> [[Lyrre T'enna]] depicted Grizmallt nerf in her [[Lyrre T'enna's annotated field guide|field guide]], as an illustration of Nerf, a group once originated on [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], but outliving its [[Destruction of Alderaan/Legends|destruction]] due to various populations having long been exported from the planet.<ref name="wildlife">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The "rangy" variation of nerfs was first depicted in [[2001]] book ''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]'', identified simply as "Nerf".<ref name="wildlife" /> They were later mentioned in ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', a [[2006]] reference book by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]].<ref name="Alien" /> They were first identified as ''Grizmallt Nerfs'' in the [[Databank (original)|Databank]] entry for nerfs published on [[StarWars.com]]<ref name="DB" />
